notice.title: Please note
notice.body: Please note: use the latest version of Firefox or Chrome; other browsers have not been tested. In other browsers the app may behave differently or give odd and possibly unreliable results.

explanation.title: Explanation
explanation.intro: Explanation: this app helps you check whether a substance is forbidden in the laboratory. A substance here means either a pure substance, i.e. one CAS RN, or a mixture, i.e. several CAS RNs. Note that a substance that is not forbidden is not necessarily allowed, because that depends on more factors. You can check a substance with one of two input methods: a file or manual input.
explanation.file: For file input you need an SDS as a PDF that contains text, so not a scanned image. Preferably use an SDS from Sigma-Aldrich; these turn out to be more complete than others. If you have trouble finding an SDS, try this Safety Data Sheet Search app. Please note: the SDS must contain at least one valid CAS RN or H code (H statements written out in full are not detected). Manual input requires at least one CAS RN or H code; P codes are optional.
explanation.reports: Each report gives a verdict on whether one substance is forbidden. If you enter several substances at once and the verdict is forbidden, you cannot tell afterwards which of the substances caused it. You can stack reports: after creating one, select an input method again to create the next. Each report can be removed with its own button. Reloading the page removes all input and reports and gives you a clean slate.

cat0.description: Not allowed, because the substance has a forbidden H code and/or is on the list of forbidden CAS RNs.

cat1.description: Temporarily allowed. Substances in this category cannot be looked up with this app (yet).

cat2.description: The substance has a forbidden H code and/or CAS RN, but is on the list of explicitly allowed substances because it is essential for lab courses, for teaching or research projects, or is used "frequently". Such a substance is tolerated.

cat3.description: Not forbidden, because the substance has no forbidden H code and is not on the list of forbidden CAS RNs.
